name: Sona BLW Precision Forgings Ltd
title: Sona BLW Precision Forgings Ltd - 543300 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

summary.headline: Sona Comstar Q2 FY27 revenue rose 35% YoY to ₹1,546 crore and EBITDA to ₹356 crore, but EBITDA margin fell to 23% on mix and input costs.
summary.overview: Q2 FY27 set company records for revenue, EBITDA and PAT, with BEV revenue up 129% YoY and above 50% of automotive revenue for the first time. Margins were lower YoY: EBITDA margin 23% (down 2.3 pp) on traction motor mix shift and West Asia-linked input inflation. Order additions of ₹36 billion (third highest quarter) took the net order book to ₹251 billion, the second highest ever. Management kept the 23-25% EBITDA margin range and flagged the Denso JV closings (JV1 targeted by end-December 2026, JV2 in 1H CY2027).

segments.name: BEV / EV business
segments.commentary: BEV revenue grew 129% YoY and 40% QoQ, and was 51% of automotive product sales in Q2; H1 BEV revenue ₹1,042 crore (+119%). Two-wheeler and three-wheeler demand in India was the main driver.

segments.name: Traction motors
segments.commentary: Business grew about 50% QoQ, faster than management expected; driven by both wallet-share gains at existing OEMs and market growth, and it is the main reason for the margin dilution.

segments.name: EV suspension motors
segments.commentary: Fastest-growing product, reported at about 7% of revenue; its order book so far is with a single customer, with other OEM talks ongoing.

segments.name: Differential assemblies and gears (DA + DG)
segments.commentary: Combined revenue up 37% YoY; all three large EV DA customers picked up in Q2. Entered ICE passenger-car differential assembly with an existing gear customer.

segments.name: Railways
segments.commentary: Air springs supplied for the first time this quarter and ramping; first batch of HVAC systems supplied in FY27; electric panels in early ramp-up.

segments.name: Geography and mix
segments.commentary: Eastern markets are about 2/3 of revenue, up from about 1/3 two years ago. Two/three-wheelers are 14% of revenue; auto vs non-auto split 70:30.

guidance_outlook: EBITDA margin range of 23-25% retained for now; management expects about 23% in a normal macro scenario and says it will hold unless oil reaches about $150.
Margin direction depends on traction motor mix (lower-margin product) and on whether material prices stay high, flat or fall.
JV1 (carve-out of business) targeted to close by end-December 2026, possibly slipping into January 2027; JV2 not yet formed, targeted for 1H CY2027.
Management reiterated a long-term aspiration implying about 25% revenue CAGR, targeting 10x growth over 10 years under Sona Comstar 2.0.

Net cash could reach roughly ₹2,800-3,000 crore by year end if the Denso JV proceeds of about ₹900 crore are received, per analyst arithmetic; management said tax, capex and JV2 capex will absorb part of this.
M&A remains selective; cash-to-EBITDA ratio ceiling of about 1.5x is the stated threshold before deploying cash.
capex_capacity: ₹62 crore of capex declared last quarter for robotics and physical AI, per management.
Helical limited slip differential, air springs for railways and rear radar sensor for two-wheelers commercialised in Q2; three new products in the quarter, a record.

Capacity and capability to ramp fast were cited in the context of traction motor demand; heavy rare earth magnets are unavailable due to Chinese export restrictions, and the company moved to light rare earth alternatives.
AMRs developed in-house are being deployed on Sona factory floors for use-case development.
Robotics and physical AI order book about 4% of the ₹251 billion total order book.
demand_pricing: Q2 order additions ₹36 billion, the third highest quarter; net order book ₹251 billion, the second highest in company history; wins spread across differentials, gears, traction motors, controllers, starter motors, sensors and railways.
Four new EPIC programs in Q2 (3 BEV, 1 intelligent and connected); 75 EPIC programs across 37 customers at end-H1, of which 44 are in production and 31 yet to start.
Inflation: steel, copper and oil derivatives rose on West Asia conflict; freight rates nearly doubled QoQ.
Pass-through contracts exist with customers but lag the input cost increases, and the percentage margin falls arithmetically when costs rise and are passed through.
Europe: OEMs seeking an alternative supply chain to China, and the company is winning more European business.
Management said it is not taking customer-specific questions.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the suspension motor growth, and what is the order pipeline?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the product's trajectory is hard to predict; the first launch customer's model underperformed then its new model exceeded expectations. Order book is still limited to one customer, with significant talks with other OEMs; no quantified pipeline given.

qa_highlights.question: Denso JV timelines?
qa_highlights.answer: JV1 (carve-out) targeted to close by end-December 2026, possibly January 2027. JV2 not yet formed, targeted for 1H CY2027.

qa_highlights.question: Why is traction motor growth above industry growth, and what is the three-wheeler contribution?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited both wallet-share gains and market growth, plus OEM supply-chain difficulties that favoured the company's agility. Three-wheeler contribution was not quantified; a further product launch is planned this quarter.

qa_highlights.question: Will margins hold at 23-25% given mix shift and inflation?
qa_highlights.answer: Management kept the 23-25% range. CFO said about 23% is the ballpark in a normal scenario and product mix is the key determinant; material price flattening would support margins, further sharp increases would hurt.

qa_highlights.question: What is the net cash position and M&A plan?
qa_highlights.answer: Gross cash ₹1,966 crore, net ₹1,400-1,500 crore. M&A is selective (three deals in the last decade), with four filters: 15-year product life, top 5-10 global position, margin and return accretion, and moral good. Cash-to-EBITDA ceiling of about 1.5x.

qa_highlights.question: Robotics and humanoid R&D spend, timelines and capex?
qa_highlights.answer: R&D is in-house, mostly staff time; ₹62 crore capex is earmarked for the area. Management will demonstrate at Bharat Expo in February 2027. No inflection year was forecast; the curve is expected to be steep when it arrives.

risks_watch: Continued margin compression from traction motor mix shift and lagged pass-through of steel, copper and oil-linked inflation, with freight costs nearly doubled QoQ.
Suspension motor growth depends on a single customer so far; other OEM wins still to be secured.
Heavy rare earth export restrictions from China remain in place with no sign of easing.
Denso JV timing could slip (JV1 into January 2027; JV2 not until 1H CY2027).
Management flagged near-term predictability as difficult due to West Asia inflation.
Railway growth outlook not quantified; depends on timely new-product launches.
summary.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on demand, orders and cash flow, with the mood set as a near-perfect quarter. More cautious on margins and input costs, where management explicitly said near-term predictability is limited and declined to give forward growth figures for railways or robotics.
key_quotes: Q2 was almost a perfect quarter for us across all metrics - financial performance, new order wins, technology and new products, cash flow generation, and our total quality management.
Traction motor demand has significantly exceeded even our own internal expectations.
And M&A is the right way to look at it. Just because everyone is doing it, is not the reason we will do it.
Whenever it does come, the curve will be very steep. That is something I can guarantee.

financial_highlights.change: +35% YoY; +18% QoQ vs previous record ₹1,310 crore
90% of H1 EBITDA; ₹44 crore working capital release
More than 50% above full FY26 FCF

adds.what: No new productive capacity (plants/lines) disclosed; company says it has capability and capacity to ramp traction motors with agility

growth.why: Management reiterated a ~25% medium-term revenue CAGR aspiration (10x in 10 years under Sona Comstar 2.0), backed by a ₹251 bn net order book (second highest ever), 75 EPIC programs across 37 customers, and Q2 revenue up 35% YoY; no new capacity quantified, so backing is partial.
